reading.body:
H.R. 9442, the Artificial Intelligence Data Center Moratorium Act, has one sponsor and nineteen cosponsors, all Democrats, and three lobbying filings naming it.

The cosponsor list is the clearest signal in the data. Every named member is from the same party, so the bill's support is not bipartisan on the record shown here. The bill's own text is tagged with energy and data centers and uses preemption language about state law, which places it in the same territory as the state and local rules on where AI compute may be built and who pays for its power.

For AI specifically, the subject is the physical layer. A moratorium on data centers is a constraint on where compute can be sited, and compute is what training and serving models consume. The two lobbying filings, from NETWORK and the Business Software Alliance, show the bill was an issue in lobbying activity. A filing that names a bill shows only that the bill was an issue, not the position the filer took.

What the data does not cover: it does not give the bill's status beyond a latest status date, does not record any vote, and does not state what the moratorium would prohibit or for how long. The lobbying counts are small, three filings, and two firms, so they describe attention rather than a campaign. Nothing here shows whether the bill has moved, stalled, or drawn opposition.

summary: H.R. 9442, Artificial Intelligence Data Center Moratorium Act. Latest status date 2026-06-24. Issues tagged from the bill's own text: energy and data centers. Its text uses preemption language about state law. 3 lobbying filing(s) for 2025 or later name it.
